question.zh: 怎么完成飞机的仿真设计？
question.en: How can aircraft simulation design be carried out?
question.domain: aircraft simulation design (conceptual design, flight dynamics, aerodynamic modeling, MDO, HIL validation)

roots.statement: Aircraft simulation design can be organized around an integrated conceptual-design and simulation-optimization environment that runs an end-to-end civil-airplane design case and uses an optimizer to minimize a design objective such as direct operating cost.
roots.scope: Applies when an integrated conceptual-design toolset and a simulation-integration optimizer are available for civil-airplane conceptual design.
roots.criteria: Evidence would include claims showing an end-to-end conceptual design system and an optimization environment minimizing a design objective within that workflow.
roots.caveat: Candidate answer generated from the merged claim graph; support counts are structural links, not a truth vote. Read the linked claims before relying on it.

links.reason: CACDS runs the CJX civil-airplane case end-to-end, evidencing an integrated conceptual-design environment.
The CJX case uses ModelCenter's Boeing Design Explorer optimizer for DOC minimization, evidencing simulation-integration optimization.
CACDS provides a unified geometry-to-analysis-to-optimization workflow, supporting an integrated end-to-end design route.
CACDS is coupled with ModelCenter as optimization engine via defined inputs/outputs, supporting simulation-optimization integration.
CACDS exposes design variables, constraints, and objectives to ModelCenter, enabling optimizer setup.
ModelCenter includes DOC-minimization and other optimization templates, supporting objective-minimizing design workflows.
The DOC-optimized concept changes wing geometry, showing the optimizer applied within the design case.
A unified modular MDO framework integrates disciplinary modules into one optimization environment, supporting integrated aircraft optimization.
The MDO framework's Level 2 module optimizes configuration geometry with objective functions, supporting the optimization-environment route.
The MDO framework's Level 2 module optimizes wing layout and planform parameters, further evidencing optimization within conceptual design.

roots.statement: Conceptual aircraft design can be pursued through a unified modular multidisciplinary design optimization framework with nested optimization levels that optimize configuration and wing-box design variables, while structural and static-margin constraints may materially affect the resulting design.
roots.scope: Applies when a modular MDO framework and appropriate structural or static-margin constraints are available for conceptual aircraft design.
roots.criteria: Evidence would include a modular MDO framework with nested optimization levels and studies showing how structural or static-margin constraints change optimized designs.
roots.caveat: Candidate answer generated from the merged claim graph; support counts are structural links, not a truth vote. Read the linked claims before relying on it.

links.reason: States the modular MDO framework has two nested optimization levels, matching the answer's core architecture.
Confirms a unified modular MDO framework integrating disciplinary modules was implemented for conceptual aircraft design.
Shows the upper nested level optimizes configuration geometric variables, supporting configuration optimization in the route.
Shows the upper nested level optimizes wing-box layout and wingtip/tip-chord variables.
Describes Level 1 performance optimizations, supporting the two-level nested optimization structure.
Reports static-margin enforcement raised gross weight about 6%, showing static-margin constraints materially change optimized design.
Shows plate-buckling constraints were included, supporting structural constraints in the MDO problem.
Finds the wing box was primarily sized by plate-buckling constraints, supporting structural constraints materially affecting design.
Limits the structural-constraint claim: this MDO problem omitted stress and displacement constraints.
Shows the displacement constraint was inactive, bounding which structural constraints materially affect this design.

roots.title_zh: 非线性飞行动力学建模
roots.statement: Aircraft simulation can be formulated as a coupled nonlinear differential-algebraic flight-dynamics model with six-degree-of-freedom equations expressed in body or wind axes, requiring state variables and parameters to be specified.
roots.scope: Applies when a physics-based flight-dynamics model is needed and the equation structure, axis system, variables, and parameters can be specified.
roots.criteria: Evidence would include claims specifying the DAE structure, axis-system equations, and variable or parameter requirements for flight-dynamics simulation.
roots.caveat: Candidate answer generated from the merged claim graph; support counts are structural links, not a truth vote. Read the linked claims before relying on it.

links.reason: Specifies the coupled 35-equation nonlinear DAE with 39 variables and 30 parameters.
Gives a wind-axis force equation, showing axis-system equation structure for flight simulation.
Gives a wind-axis scalar equation, supporting velocity-axis formulation of flight dynamics.
Gives a wind-axis angle-of-attack equation, supporting axis-system simulation equations.
Expresses body-axis angular rates from Euler angles, specifying state-variable relation.
Provides body-axis rotational acceleration equations, supporting six-DOF equation structure.
States forward-simulation input variables needed for a unique solution.
Constrains input specification to inverse-simulation mode with trajectory coordinates plus one variable.
Limits reduced moment equations to left-right symmetric airplanes.
Describes real-time simulation computing aircraft dynamics differential equations.

roots.statement: Simulation-model fidelity can be improved by identifying aerodynamic delta or parameter models from flight-test or simulated doublet data and updating the original aerodynamic database, followed by checking predictions against measured flight parameters.
roots.scope: Applies when test or simulated maneuver data are available for identifying aerodynamic increments or parameters and updating an existing simulation model.
roots.criteria: Evidence would include identification of aerodynamic increments or parameters from test data and reported improvement of simulation predictions after updating the model.
roots.caveat: Candidate answer generated from the merged claim graph; support counts are structural links, not a truth vote. Read the linked claims before relying on it.

links.reason: Reports estimating a delta aerodynamic model from flight data for simulation updating.
Gives identified ΔC_X delta-model parameters from flight-test maneuvers.
Gives identified ΔC_Z delta-model parameters from flight-test maneuvers.
Gives identified ΔC_m delta-model parameters from flight-test maneuvers.
Describes estimated delta aerodynamic models for longitudinal coefficients used to update simulation.
States augmented aerodynamic database significantly improves flight-parameter predictions.
Reports independent flight-test validation of the updated model's improvement.
Shows updated model closely matches measured angle of attack, pitch, and altitude.
Shows original model deviates from measured flight profiles, motivating data-based calibration.
Describes parameter identification from simulated elevator-doublet data reproducing longitudinal coefficients.

roots.statement: Before flight test, aircraft simulation design can be validated through real-time hardware-in-the-loop testing in which a ground computer solves the aircraft dynamics and the integrated control and propulsion systems are exercised under specified tracking-error criteria.
roots.scope: Applies when a real-time HIL test platform and integrated control or propulsion components are available for pre-flight evaluation.
roots.criteria: Evidence would include a real-time HIL system computing aircraft dynamics, integrated control or propulsion operation, and reported tracking or stability results supporting pre-flight evaluation.
roots.caveat: Candidate answer generated from the merged claim graph; support counts are structural links, not a truth vote. Read the linked claims before relying on it.

links.reason: Ground computer solving aircraft dynamics each cycle directly instantiates the real-time HIL computational core.
HIL system running stably before flight test directly supports pre-flight validation.
Engine control with specified permissible tracking errors directly supports tracking-error validation in HIL.
Integrated flight control and propulsion operating effectively supports exercising integrated systems in HIL validation.
Reported attitude stability in joint HIL supports validation via stability results.
Successful reference trajectory tracking in joint HIL supports validation via tracking results.
Closed-loop HIL platform integrating flight control, propulsion, simulation equipment, and database supports the validation route.
Hardware set including flight control computer, engine controller/simulator, and ground computer supports HIL validation setup.
Low-cost workflow combining dynamics model, autopilot, and SITL/HITL testing supports HIL validation as a method.
HIL-versus-flight discrepancies around 10% bound the fidelity/accuracy claim for HIL validation.
